close_reason: Superseded by sibling beads: (1) /query filter+sort ignored — IMPLEMENTED in JMAP-826m.4 (commit 92b46ac), MemoryBackend now applies typed filter and sort. (2) /queryChanges filter+sort ignored — DISCLOSED in memory.rs module doc by JMAP-826m.4, fix tracked at JMAP-ya7g. (3) update_object server-set-field echo gap — tracked separately at JMAP-826m.6. Bead .10's recommended remediation (implement OR loudly document) has been applied to all three concerns: implementation for (1), disclosure-plus-follow-up-bead for (2), and (3) is its own ready bead. The meta-risk bead concern about contributors copying gaps is reduced because the module doc now has a complete 'what is and is not implemented' list.
description:
Scenario: A downstream contributor reads memory.rs:5-13 ('reference implementation', 'for downstream contributors to study') and copies the MemoryBackend pattern into their own postgres-backed MetadataBackend. They notice query_objects is a stub that ignores filter and sort, conclude this is the workspace pattern, and ship a backend that silently ignores their clients' filter args. This becomes a class of issue reports against THEIR product, and the bug-vector trail leads back to this crate's 'reference implementation'.

The Metadata-specific behaviour list (memory.rs:26-41) discloses 4 limitations (uniqueness, maySetPrivate, quota, related-object validation). It does NOT disclose:
- /query: filter ignored (memory.rs:566-614 has _filter, _sort)
- /query: sort ignored
- /queryChanges: filter+sort ignored (delegates to get_changes which doesn't filter either)
- update_object: never reports Some(obj) server-set-field echo

The Single-user limitation section (memory.rs:43-83) is well-written and handles principal_id correctly. The /query/sort gap deserves the same treatment.

Maintenance consequence: every contributor who reads this as a reference will reproduce the same gap. The crate gets a reputation for 'JMAP that says it supports filtering but actually returns everything'. Fixing the docs is cheap; fixing the reputation later is expensive.

Resolution options:
(a) Implement minimal filter + sort in MemoryBackend (matches §3.4 spec floor, ~100 lines).
(b) Add a loud 'Metadata-specific behaviour' bullet documenting these gaps before someone copies the pattern.
title: MemoryBackend mass-claims 'reference implementation' but lacks /query filter/sort, /query position correctness, server-set-field echo on update — contributors WILL copy this and inherit the gaps
